ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.notes: peeled and cut into thin rounds or matchstick strips

ingredients.name: Green chillies
ingredients.notes: slit; this is a mild curry so green chilli is preferred over red chilli powder

ingredients.name: Unroasted Sri Lankan curry powder
ingredients.notes: just a small amount -- this is meant to be a mild curry

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: 1/2 cup, or use thin coconut milk for a richer result

ingredients.name: Thick coconut milk
ingredients.notes: 3/4 cup; the creamy coconut milk base is the dish's defining character

steps.instruction: Peel the carrots and cut into thin rounds or thin matchstick strips. Thinner pieces cook faster and absorb more flavour.

Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds, fenugreek, and cumin seeds (if using) and let them splutter. Add curry leaves, pandan leaf, and cinnamon stick and sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion, garlic, and green chillies. Saute until the onion softens, about 3 minutes.

Add the carrot pieces, turmeric, curry powder, and salt. Toss to coat. Add the water (or thin coconut milk). Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the carrots are just tender.
Pour in the thick coconut milk. Stir gently and simmer uncovered on low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent curdling, until the gravy thickens to a creamy consistency.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice alongside a spicier meat or fish curry -- carrot curry is intentionally mild and is often paired with spicier dishes to balance the meal.

source_site: islandsmile.org, cross-checked against theflavorbender.com, foodcnr.com, topsrilankanrecipe.com, serendibkitchen.com, olivemagazine.com, angiesrecipes.blogspot.com, and hillvale.co.uk
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources; very strong agreement on the mild, coconut-milk-dominant character and the thin-then-thick coconut milk technique
notes: Carrot curry (also called carrot kirata) is one of the mildest curries in the Sri Lankan repertoire and is explicitly described by islandsmile.org as suitable for toddlers. theflavorbender.com makes an important observation: this is a 'dump and cook' recipe in many households -- the vegetables, spices, and thin coconut milk are combined in one pot from the start without any initial sauteing, and the thick coconut milk is added at the end. This entry reflects the more common tempered version, but the simplified no-temper version is equally valid and authentic. Carrot curry is almost always served alongside a spicier dish (chicken curry, fish curry, or dhal curry) since it is designed to be a mild, sweet counterpoint in a rice-and-curry spread.
